text:
ashwin: heads-up — prod p99 for /v1/streams jumped ~180ms after today's runtime deploy, not just a tiny blip. saw it at ~11:02 UTC.

maria: yep seeing it on the dashboards, SSE endpoints specifically. p50 stable, p95 +40ms, p99 +180ms.

jess: CI perf job 'sse_stream_micro' failed on staging with +12% p95 earlier this morning. logs attached to the job.

oliver: I pulled a few traces — most time is spent in serialization/toolcall handoff. stack shows Encoder::encode -> json::to_vec -> thread pool wait.

kai: interesting — KV prefetch traces show a burst of synchronous tool calls around the same time as serialization spikes. could be contention.

ashwin: I started a quick bisect locally. suspect change that touched framing/proto defaults in runtime merge 5173 (the compact framing swap) — it added a new step that writes an intermediate buffer and calls flush more often.

maria: can you paste the repro steps? I can run perf harness against staging.

ashwin: repro pattern I used: 1) open SSE connection, 2) send 40 short streaming requests concurrently (seq len ~64), 3) measure time from first chunk to final chunk. I used:
```bash
./bench --endpoint https://staging.redwood/api/stream --concurrency 40 --msgs 40 --seq 64
```
results show repeated 10-30ms extra per-request delay attributed to 'frame flush' in traces.

oliver: ran pprof on a few captured profiles from staging: hot path is in proto framing write path taking syscalls due to small writes. coalescing got worse after framing tweak.

jess: CI artifacts: staging-perf/2026-03-18/sse_stream_micro.html — p95 diff +12%, p99 +18%. tagging it here.

ashwin: proposal: pause the rollout to 100% and revert the framing change until we have a fix for write coalescing. can we do a staged revert?

ci-bot: deployment "runtime-v3.9.0" currently at 45% rollout. pausing rollout per @ashwin.

maria: I can test a local revert patch that reuses the previous framing buffer strategy (single write for header+payload) and run the bench. will post numbers shortly.

kai: also worth noting batching heuristics: the change that flips to compact framing also updated the batcher to prefer smaller batches for low-latency. that increases syscall frequency under micro loads. Might be two orthogonal effects compounding.

oliver: good catch — I instrumented the batcher: when concurrency < 50 and seq len < 128 it now emits batches of size 1-3 rather than 8-16. makes sense we see more small writes.

ashwin: mitigation options: 1) revert framing + batching tweak, 2) adjust Nagle/coalesce in SSE writer to buffer up to X bytes/timeout, 3) optimize json encoder path to avoid threadpool hop for tiny payloads.

maria: I ran the revert locally (branch: revert/compact-framing) — microbench shows p99 back to baseline and p95 delta goes away. sharing numbers in 5m.

jess: sounds like revert is low-risk and buys time for a proper fix. we should also add an automated microbenchmark gate for the CI perf job to catch this class of change.

ashwin: agreed. I'll open a revert PR and add the CI gate (sse_stream_micro must not regress >5% p95). tagging @oliver for follow-up optimizations.

oliver: I'll follow up on encoder threadpool hop and see if we can make tiny payload path inline encode on the caller stack to avoid wakeups.

sre-bot: incident ticket created: INF-2026-143 — "SSE serialization/coalesce latency spike after runtime deploy". escalation: P2.

ashwin: thanks all. next steps: 1) push revert PR and hold rollout, 2) add CI microbenchmark threshold, 3) oliver + kai to investigate encoder inline path and batcher heuristics. will update in this thread with numbers. :thumbsup:
